profiles.field_rule: Research trial: Bahia grass commonly makes two V-like racemes above a mat-forming or rhizomatous turf base. diagnostic_checks.check: Usually two nearly paired racemes at the summit, occasionally a third; each roughly 4–12(–15) cm in the Flora
Mat-forming rhizomatous perennial, with flowering culms typically about 20–75 cm in the regional Flora
Broadly ovate to obovate glabrous spikelets, usually 2.5–3.8 mm across modern treatments
Lower glume typically absent or poorly developed, upper glume smooth and about as long as the spikelet
Short ligule with hairs described in POWO accounts; examine exact collar rather than inferring from turf

diagnostic_review.note: Paired racemes strongly support Bahia grass but microscopic broadly ovate glumes and seed size not confirmed; many records from lawns and could be introduced turf.

profiles.field_rule: Research trial: cultivated oat has an often drooping open panicle of large oat spikelets, generally without conspicuous awns; some varieties have weak awns. Distinguish wild oat by mature floret callus hairs and disarticulation, not just a hanging oat-shaped head. Check crop or seed-mix origin.

diagnostic_checks.check: Open often drooping panicle with large pendulous oat spikelets
Usually 1–2 fertile florets in hulled oats, but substantially more in some naked-oat types; normal spikelets commonly 25–32 mm long
Floret calluses generally glabrous or with very short hairs, unlike conspicuously bearded wild oat calluses
In cultivated oats, ripe florets generally stay attached to one another instead of easily breaking below each floret
Lemmas typically awnless but sometimes carry weakly bent awns; absence of awns alone is not a species proof

diagnostic_review.note: Cultivated oats versus wild oats/forage mixtures and naturally established populations not determined.
